definitions.explanation: A simple Japanese breakfast dish consisting of a raw egg mixed into hot steamed rice, typically seasoned with soy sauce.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}ご{飯|はん}は{卵|たまご}かけご{飯|はん}にしよう。
examples.english: Let's have raw egg on rice for breakfast.

examples.japanese: {卵|たまご}かけご{飯|はん}には{新鮮|しんせん}な{卵|たまご}を{使|つか}った{方|ほう}がいい。
examples.english: It's better to use fresh eggs for raw egg rice.

examples.japanese: {醤油|しょうゆ}をかけた{卵|たまご}かけご{飯|はん}は{最高|さいこう}だ。
examples.english: Raw egg on rice with soy sauce is the best.

notes:
WORD STRUCTURE:
{卵|たまご} (egg) + かけ (from {掛|か}ける, to pour over) + ご{飯|はん} (rice, meal)

ABBREVIATION:
Often abbreviated as TKG ({T}amago {K}ake {G}ohan), especially in casual conversation and on social media. Some restaurants even use TKG on their menus.

HOW TO MAKE:
1. Crack a raw egg into a bowl of hot steamed rice
2. Add soy sauce to taste
3. Mix thoroughly until the egg coats the rice

VARIATIONS:
・{卵黄|らんおう}だけを{使|つか}う - using only the yolk
・{白身|しろみ}を{泡立|あわだ}てる - whipping the egg white
・だし{醤油|じょうゆ}を{使|つか}う - using dashi soy sauce
・ごま{油|あぶら}を{加|くわ}える - adding sesame oil

FOOD SAFETY NOTE:
In Japan, eggs are produced and handled with strict hygiene standards that make eating them raw relatively safe. This dish is less common in countries where eggs are not produced to the same standards.

SIMILAR DISHES:
・{卵焼|たまごや}きご{飯|はん} - rice with tamagoyaki (cooked omelet)
・{目玉焼|めだまや}き{丼|どん} - rice bowl with fried egg
・{親子丼|おやこどん} - chicken and egg rice bowl
